chunks: Saad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The prayer of Zaf (marching forward) while on the back is a nod of the head with a Takbir; Al-Musayafah is a Takbir with a nod; Al-Mutaradah is a nod; each man prays facing his own direction.

And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah and Ayub ibn Nuh, from Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah, who said: Some of our companions narrated to me from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The minimum that suffices in the measure of Al-Musayafah regarding the Takbir is two Takbirs for each prayer, except for the Maghrib prayer, for it has three.
ai.seo_question: What are the specific rules and minimum requirements for performing prayer while marching or swimming according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the jurisprudence of *Salat al-Musayafah* (prayer while swimming or in water) and *Salat al-Zahf* (prayer while marching), emphasizing the flexibility of prostration through head nodding (*I'ima'*) when full bowing is impractical. It establishes that each individual prays facing their own direction (*Qibla*) independently, reflecting the Shia principle of accommodating physical constraints in ritual worship. The text further clarifies the minimum ritual requirements, specifying two Takbirs for Musayafah and three for Maghrib, highlighting the pragmatic adaptation of prayer forms in dynamic or challenging environments.
